chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from Al-Halabi, that he said:

Regarding a man who says, 'If I die, my slave is free,' and there is a debt upon the man: He said, 'If he dies and there is a debt upon him that has encompassed the value of the slave, the slave is sold; and if it has not encompassed the value of the slave, the slave is asked to work (to earn) to pay the debt of his master, and he is free once he pays it.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to a slave who is freed by will but has outstanding debts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the priority of debt repayment in the emancipation process, establishing that a slave's labor or sale value is first applied to settle the master's debts before freedom is granted. It reflects the Shia juristic principle that financial obligations take precedence over the immediate execution of a manumission bequest, ensuring creditors are satisfied. The ruling highlights the practical balance between honoring the owner's wish for the slave's freedom and maintaining economic justice through debt settlement.
